item.title: Decode one instruction: 31 C9
item.description:
Target: Windows x86-64.
Decode this instruction (hex bytes):
31 C9
What is the assembly, and why do compilers emit it? What happens to `rcx`?
---
## Answer
`xor ecx, ecx`
- `31` = `XOR r/m32, r32`; ModRM `C9` = `11 001 001` → mod=11 (register-direct), reg=ecx, rm=ecx, so both operands are the same register. - x ^ x = 0, so it zeroes `ecx` in 2 bytes (vs 5 for `mov ecx, 0`), and CPUs treat it as a dependency-breaking zero idiom. - Writing a 32-bit register zero-extends into the upper half, so the whole of `rcx` becomes 0 — no REX.W needed.
